title: A SkyLink bridge only becomes usable after third-party audit results are formalized by a Sky Core Executive Vote
content:
The Token SkyLink setup sequence puts security review on both sides of deployment. Before any code ships, A.2.2.8.1.1.1.1.3 requires the Prime Agent to engage "a reputable third-party security audit firm," negotiate scope, timeline and fees, and document projected development, audit and deployment costs for later reimbursement.

After deployment, A.2.2.8.1.1.1.3.1 has the Agent share "the Token SkyLink contract's final address with the audit firm for verification," Operational GovOps confirm that "the bridge contract address and references match the updated Prime Agent Artifact," and the audit firm "update the bridging audit registry with the results of the audit." Only then does A.2.2.8.1.1.1.3.2 apply the final gate: "Core GovOps formalizes the audit results with a Sky Core Executive Vote to fully activate bridging functionality."

The address-verification step is the subtle one. Auditing source code proves nothing about what was actually deployed, so the firm is asked to confirm the live address, and GovOps to confirm it matches the Artifact. That closes the gap between what was reviewed, what was deployed, and what the Atlas says exists.

The Executive Vote placement is also deliberate: the Agent's own token holders approved the plan earlier (A.2.2.8.1.1.1.2.2), but activation of a bridge that Sky Core will own and all Agents will share requires ecosystem-level consent. Activation is simultaneously what starts volume tracking in the Reimbursement Module, so the Agent's cost recovery cannot begin before Sky Core has accepted the audit.
description: The audit firm is engaged before deployment, verifies the deployed contract address, and files results to a bridging audit registry; Core GovOps then activates bridging by Executive Vote.
